note.explanation: For a neutral atom, the atomic number tells you the number of protons and electrons. The mass number counts protons and neutrons together. Subtract the atomic number from the mass number to find the neutrons.
examples: For ¹³⁷₅₆Ba: protons = 56, electrons = 56, and neutrons = 137 − 56 = 81.
note.simple: Atomic number is the proton count. Mass number is protons plus neutrons. So, neutrons = mass number − atomic number.

explain.title: Atomic number
explain.body: The number of protons present in the atoms of an element is always fixed and it is called the atomic number of that element. It is represented by Z. The atomic number identifies the element.

explain.title: Mass number
explain.body: The total number of protons and neutrons present in an atom almost accounts for the total mass of that atom and hence it is called its nucleon number or mass number. It is represented by A. Electrons are not included in the mass number.

explain.title: Reading the atom symbol
explain.body: The atomic number is written as a left subscript while the mass number as a left superscript. For example, in ¹⁶₈O, A = 16 and Z = 8.

explain.title: Finding the particles
explain.body: For a neutral atom, electrons equal protons, so both counts equal Z. The number of neutrons is found using N = A − Z.

mistakes: Do not confuse the upper-left mass number A with the lower-left atomic number Z.
Do not count electrons in the mass number; it is the total of protons and neutrons.
Do not say that atomic number is the number of neutrons; it is the number of protons.
When finding neutrons, subtract Z from A, not A from Z.
For a neutral atom, do not give different numbers of protons and electrons.
